newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Gendarmes hold five Western aid workers in Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Gendarmes hold five Western aid workers in Zaire.

text.p: Five Western relief workers who landed a small plane in the heart of the Zairean jungle for refuelling have been held by local gendarmes since Wednesday, diplomats and aidworkers said on Saturday.

Three Frenchmen, one American missionary in Zaire since 1950, and one British man were being held in the town of Ikela, they told Reuters. The five work for missionary and non-governmental organisations Atlas, Merlin and Frodesa.
Zaire's military authorities were sending a plane to ensure their release and bring them back to Kinshasa, an aidworker said.

"They were on a mission to see how they could approach Ubundu and stopped at Ikela for refuelling and to meet the local authorities. We don't know why they are being held," Jean Louis Lapierre, director of Atlas logistics, a transport NGO said.
"After the U.N. evacuation from Kisangani, we wanted to study the logistical possibilities of getting food to the refugees but it has not taken place in the spirit we wished."
U.N. agencies and NGOs evacuated Zaire's third city Kisangani a week ago complaining of harassment by local military authorities and degenerating security.
The Zairean authorities have directed tens of thousands refugees to Ubundu after they fled Tingi Tingi refugee camp to the south east in the face of a rebel advance.
Ubundu is 100 km (60 miles) south of Kisangani, the refugees first destination, and 300 km (190 miles) east of Ikela.
Lapierre said Ikela, 300 km south west of Kisangani, was a possible rear base for delivery of food and medical aid.
